name: Doolittle raid
kicker: First U.S. air raid on Japan’s home islands · A 1942 morale boost
briefing: Four months after Pearl Harbor, 16 U.S. Army B-25 bombers did something that had never been tried in combat: they took off from the deck of the aircraft carrier USS _Hornet_ and bombed Tokyo and other Japanese cities. Led by Lieutenant Colonel Jimmy Doolittle, the April 18, 1942, raid did little damage, and every plane was lost, but it lifted American spirits and pushed Japan’s leaders to approve the plan that led to the Battle of Midway.
answerHtml: Doolittle Raid (or Tokyo Raid; prompt on Doolittle alone or on bombing of Tokyo; do not accept “Pearl Harbor” or “Battle of Midway”)
reject: atomic bombings of hiroshima and nagasaki

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Franklin Roosevelt joked to reporters that the bombers in this raid had taken off from “Shangri-La,” the hidden paradise in the novel _Lost Horizon_, and the Navy later gave that name to a new aircraft carrier.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this April 1942 raid in which B-25 bombers launched from the USS _Hornet_ struck Tokyo.

tossups.p: Captain Marc Mitscher commanded the aircraft carrier that carried this raid’s planes, which sailed toward Japan with a second carrier group led by William Halsey aboard the _Enterprise_. Together the ships formed Task Force 16.
tossups.r: Its sixteen B-25 bombers took off from the USS _Hornet_. For 10 points, name this April 1942 attack on Tokyo.

tossups.p: To fool enemy fighter pilots, crews in this raid stuck painted broomsticks out of their bombers’ tails to look like machine guns. The pilots had practiced very short takeoffs at Eglin Field in Florida with help from a Navy flight instructor.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this April 1942 attack, the first time U.S. Army bombers flew off an aircraft carrier on a combat mission.

tossups.p: Jacob DeShazer, one of eight airmen captured by Japanese forces after this raid, later returned to Japan as a Christian missionary. Of those eight prisoners, three were executed and one died in captivity before the war ended.
tossups.r: Most of the other airmen escaped through China with help from Chinese villagers and soldiers. For 10 points, name this April 1942 bombing attack on Tokyo.

tossups.p: After this raid, Japanese troops launched the Zhejiang-Jiangxi [“juh-JYAHNG jyahng-SHEE”] campaign in eastern China, punishing towns whose people had helped American airmen and killing huge numbers of Chinese civilians. The troops also wrecked the airfields where the bombers had planned to land.
tossups.r: Most of the raiders had come down in China. For 10 points, name this April 1942 American air raid on Japan’s capital.

tossups.p: Running low on fuel, one crew in this raid flew to the Soviet Union instead of China, landing near Vladivostok [“vlad-ih-VOSS-tok”]. The Soviets, who were not at war with Japan, held the five men for more than a year.
tossups.r: All sixteen planes in this raid were lost. For 10 points, name this April 1942 attack that lifted American spirits after Pearl Harbor.

tossups.p: Survivors of this raid held reunions with a set of 80 silver goblets, turning one upside down for each man who had died. The last surviving member, Richard Cole, who had been the copilot of the lead plane, died in 2019 at age 103.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1942 attack in which B-25s took off from the USS _Hornet_ to bomb Tokyo.

tossups.p: The leader of this raid had earned a doctorate in aeronautics from MIT and, in 1929, made the first flight flown entirely by instruments, taking off and landing with his cockpit covered by a hood.
tossups.r: He received the Medal of Honor for leading this raid. For 10 points, name this bombing of Tokyo in April 1942.

tossups.p: The commander of this raid thought he would be court-martialed for losing every one of his planes. Instead, he was promoted two ranks, skipping colonel to become a brigadier general, and later commanded the Eighth Air Force in Europe.
tossups.r: Franklin Roosevelt gave him the Medal of Honor. For 10 points, name this April 1942 bombing of Japan’s capital.

tossups.p: Pilot Ted Lawson, whose bomber in this raid was nicknamed the _Ruptured Duck_, was badly hurt when it crash-landed in the water off the coast of China, and he later wrote a best-selling memoir about the mission.
tossups.r: That book became the 1944 film _Thirty Seconds Over Tokyo_, starring Spencer Tracy. For 10 points, name this 1942 attack on Japan.

tossups.p: After a Japanese picket boat spotted the American ships carrying this raid’s bombers, the cruiser _Nashville_ sank it, but the planes had to take off hours early and much farther from Japan than planned, leaving them short of fuel.
tossups.r: The bombers could not land back on their carrier, so they flew on toward China. For 10 points, name this April 1942 air attack on Japan.

tossups.p: The 2001 movie _Pearl Harbor_ ends with this raid, with Alec Baldwin playing its leader. In real life, this raid came just nine days after American and Filipino troops on the Bataan Peninsula surrendered to Japan.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this April 18, 1942, attack, the first American air raid on Japan’s home islands.

tossups.p: This raid used B-25 bombers, which were named for Billy Mitchell, an early champion of air power who had been court-martialed in 1925 for criticizing military leaders. Planners chose that model because it could take off in a short space.
tossups.r: Sixteen of them flew off the USS _Hornet_ to bomb Tokyo, Yokohama, Nagoya, Kobe, and Osaka. For 10 points, name this April 1942 attack.

tossups.p: The leader of this raid was already famous for winning air races, including the Schneider Trophy seaplane race in 1925, the first Bendix Trophy cross-country race in 1931, and the Thompson Trophy in 1932.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this raid in which that pilot led sixteen B-25s off the USS _Hornet_ to bomb Japan in April 1942.

tossups.p: This raid helped convince Japan’s leaders to approve Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto’s plan to capture a distant Pacific atoll and lure out the U.S. Navy’s carriers, hoping to keep American forces farther from their home islands.
tossups.r: That plan led to the Battle of Midway in June 1942. For 10 points, name this April 1942 American air attack on Tokyo.

clues.t: April 18, 1942: the first U.S. air attack on Japan’s home islands, hitting Tokyo
Sixteen Army B-25 bombers took off from the aircraft carrier USS _Hornet_
Boosted American morale four months after the attack on Pearl Harbor
Its leader, a famous racing pilot, received the Medal of Honor from Franklin Roosevelt
Helped convince Japan’s leaders to approve Isoroku Yamamoto’s plan, which led to the Battle of Midway (June 1942)
All 16 planes were lost: 15 came down in China, and one landed in the Soviet Union
The bombers could not land back on the carrier, so the plan was to fly on to airfields in China
Also bombed Yokohama, Nagoya, Kobe, and Osaka
_Thirty Seconds Over Tokyo_: pilot Ted Lawson’s memoir (1943) and the 1944 film starring Spencer Tracy
First time U.S. Army bombers took off from an aircraft carrier on a combat mission
Most of the 80 airmen escaped through China with help from Chinese villagers and soldiers
FDR joked the planes came from “Shangri-La” (from the novel _Lost Horizon_); the Navy later named a carrier _Shangri-La_
Captain Marc Mitscher commanded the _Hornet_; William Halsey’s _Enterprise_ group joined it in Task Force 16
Crews practiced short takeoffs at Eglin Field, Florida, and mounted painted broomsticks as fake tail guns
A Japanese picket boat spotted the ships, so the bombers took off hours early and farther from Japan than planned
Japan captured eight airmen: three were executed, one died in captivity, and four survived the war
Captured raider Jacob DeShazer later returned to Japan as a Christian missionary
Zhejiang-Jiangxi campaign: Japanese troops punished Chinese towns that had helped the raiders, killing huge numbers of civilians
One crew landed near Vladivostok; the Soviet Union, not at war with Japan, held the five men for over a year
Reunions used 80 silver goblets, one turned over for each man who died; the last raider, Richard Cole, died in 2019
Its leader had a doctorate from MIT and made the first flight flown entirely by instruments (1929)
Its leader thought he would be court-martialed but was promoted two ranks to brigadier general
Its leader won the Schneider Trophy (1925), the first Bendix Trophy (1931), and the Thompson Trophy (1932)
Ted Lawson’s plane, the _Ruptured Duck_, crash-landed in the water off the coast of China
The B-25 was named for Billy Mitchell, the air-power champion court-martialed in 1925
Came nine days after U.S. and Filipino troops surrendered on Bataan; the 2001 film _Pearl Harbor_ ends with it (Alec Baldwin as its leader)

trap.title: Raid, man, or battle?
trap.body: Tossups about this raid are full of clues that belong to other answer lines. Jimmy Doolittle, the pilot who led it, is a person, so saying just “Doolittle” earns a prompt when the question asks for the raid. The attack on Pearl Harbor (December 1941) and the Battle of Midway (June 1942) come up in the same questions, and the 1945 firebombing of Tokyo was a different, much later attack.
trap.fix: Listen for the noun: “this raid,” “this attack,” or “this mission” wants the Doolittle Raid; “this pilot” or “this general” wants Jimmy Doolittle; “this battle” at a Pacific atoll wants Midway. April 1942, the USS _Hornet_, B-25s, and _Thirty Seconds Over Tokyo_ all mean the raid.
trap.line: Real answer line: Doolittle Raid (or Tokyo Raid; prompt on Doolittle alone or on bombing of Tokyo; do not accept “Pearl Harbor” or “Battle of Midway”)
